subject: [ACME] Mutual Action Plan recap and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + discovery follow-up / mutual action plan

Hi Samir 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) attached. High-level notes: 

- Pain points: production latency spikes on peak batch processing, high per-token cost for embeddings-based search, lack of canary deploy process for model rollouts.
- Goals: reduce 95th percentile latency by 40%, cut embedding costs by ~30% through caching and quantization, and introduce a predictable rollout path with A/B canaries for model updates.
- Success metrics: p95 < 250ms for user-facing generation, embedding cost < $0.005/vector for core search workload, zero-severity regression during canary rollout.

Proposed next steps (see attached MAP):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/ML team  week of Apr 12
2) Proof-of-concept (private deployment)  4 weeks from kickoff
3) Procurement / procurement checklist & contract draft  target signature by May 25

I've attached a draft MAP (acme-mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx) that outlines milestones, owners, and target dates. Please review and fill in missing stakeholders/timing on your side.

Cc'ing Neha (solutions) who can run the tech deep-dive and Rishi (sales engineering) will be available for the POC architecture.

Open questions from our side:
- Which embedding model variants are you currently using in prod (name + average vector size)?
- Do you have any existing KV caching layers we should be aware of?

Thanks  looking forward to next steps.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment: acme-mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Gomez <laura.gomez@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery follow-up / mutual action plan

Thanks Marissa  helpful summary. A few updates from our side: 

- Confirmed pain: our search service sees sharp cost increases during end-of-month reindexing windows; embedding cost is a big contributor.
- Stakeholders to add to MAP: Alex Rios (Director, ML Platforms), Priya Shah (Head of Procurement), and Laura (Legal). I'm looping Laura and procurement on this thread.
- Timeline constraints: our Q2 budget reviews close Apr 30; if we can get a signed SOW by May 20 it's likely to be in this quarter's allocation.

I've attached our procurement timeline and a short doc with preferred contract terms. We'll need a copy of the standard SLA and a simple statement on data retention for vector cache.

Quick answers: we use a tuned variant of openembedding-1024; average vector size is 1024 dims. We have a Redis-backed cache for prefix/KV, but it's not integrated with embeddings yet.

Next best steps from my side:
- Tech deep-dive with Alex + ML infra (please propose 2 slots Apr 13-15)
- Rishi/Neha to coordinate on POC architecture and any network/secret requirements
- Procurement to review Redwood contract and SLA (cc Priya)

Thanks  Samir
Samir Khan
Head of Search & Recommendations
ACME Corp
samir.khan@acme.com | +1 (617) 555-0192

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + discovery follow-up / mutual action plan

Hi Samir  great context, thanks. Quick technical clarifications before the deep-dive: 

- For the POC we recommend starting with our 16GB A100-backed Dedicated pool to get representative latency; we can size down once we have sequence-length distributions.
- We can integrate prefix/KV caching with your Redis via our cache adapter; we'll need a short network diagram and whether Redis is accessible from a VPC peering or via an internal endpoint.
- On embeddings: we can run a two-step eval (quality + throughput) comparing your tuned openembedding-1024 vs. our optimized quantized-openembed-1024. Expected cost delta captured in MAP.

For availability, I'm free Apr 13 10:00-12:00 PT and Apr 14 14:00-16:00 PT for a 60m session with Alex + team  does either work?

I'll prepare a short POC checklist (network, secrets, sample dataset, evaluation metrics) and attach our standard SLA for procurement (redwood-sla.pdf).

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
